Based on the provided query results, I can analyze the relationship between high GDP per capita countries and their reported negative affects.

Analysis:

The data shows that while some high-GDP-per-capita countries (like Armenia at $9.67 billion) do report higher negative affects, there isn't a clear inverse correlation between these two metrics. The highest negative affect recorded is 0.705 in Syria ($8.58 billion GDP), which is significantly higher than any of the listed high-GDP-per-capita countries.

Key findings:

1. High-GDP-per-capital countries do not necessarily have lower levels of negative affects.
2. In fact, some of the highest GDP per capita countries (Bahrain at $10.75 billion) and moderate-high GDP countries (Iran varying between $9.54-$9.63 billion) report relatively low negative affects.

Conclusion:
The data suggests that high GDP per capita countries do not necessarily experience higher levels of negative affects. In fact, the highest negative affect observed in this dataset is associated with a country at a lower end of the GDP range (Syria at $8.58 billion).
